lines.say: Who lives longest in the Middle East?
Sixty years of World Bank data. Eleven countries.
Israel starts on top, at seventy two years. Lebanon is next.
Nineteen seventy five. Civil war in Lebanon. It drops eight years.
Two thousand five. The UAE overtakes Israel.
Syria's civil war costs ten years.
Then the pandemic hits the Gulf.
Twenty twenty three. The Palestinian territories drop eleven years, the year the war began.
lines.screen: West Bank and Gaza: *11 years* down in 2023

lines.say: The runner up ends less than half a year behind. The third, less than one.
lines.screen: Gold and silver: less than *half a year* apart

lines.say: If you like Israel facts, follow <<n|oʊ|ˈ|ɑ|m>> <<ˈ|r|ɑː|z>> for more.
And the top of the table?
Israel. Eighty three point two years.

caption_en:
The lead changed hands 8 times in 60 years. Guess who holds it now.

Who lives longest in the Middle East? Life expectancy at birth, World Bank, 2023:
Israel 83.2
UAE 82.9
Qatar 82.4
Lebanon 77.8
Jordan 77.8
Iran 77.7
Turkey 77.2
Iraq 72.3
Syria 72.1
Egypt 71.6
West Bank and Gaza 65.2 (76.7 in 2022)

On the way: Lebanon fell 8 years in its civil war, Iraq slid through the 1980s, the UAE passed Israel around 2005, Syria lost 10 years in its civil war, Qatar led in 2019, and the pandemic hit the Gulf in 2020 and 2021.
Not in the race: Saudi Arabia 78.7 (World Bank 2023); Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman are also under 82 (UN 2023).

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, SP.DYN.LE00.IN, 1961 to 2023. The animation interpolates between data points. AI voice.
caption_he: מי חי הכי הרבה במזרח התיכון? ישראל, 83.2 שנים (הבנק העולמי, 2023). איחוד האמירויות פחות מחצי שנה מאחור, וקטאר פחות משנה.
